kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-01.title: Cross-multiply
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-01.body:
For $x\ne0$ the equation is equivalent to $x^4=9$, i.e. $x^2=3$ (as $x^2\ge0$). So $x=\pm\sqrt3$: **2** real solutions.

**Answer: (C) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-02.title: Horizontal plus vertical
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-02.body:
Seen from above, the ant's path is still the straight segment $AB$ of length 5 m, whatever the angles of the obstacles.

Vertically, she climbs 1 m onto the first obstacle and 1 m onto the second, then comes down 1 m and 1 m: 4 m in total.

Path length: $5+4 = 9$ m.

**Answer: (B) 9 m**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-03.title: Product of numbers just below 1
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-03.body:
Both $a$ and $b$ lie between $\frac34$ and 1, close to 1. Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes a positive number smaller, so $ab<a$ and $ab<b$; this rules out $r$, $s$ and $t$.

With $a\approx0.9$ and $b\approx0.95$ we get $ab\approx0.85$ — a little below $a$, a little above $\frac34$, far from $p\approx0.1$. That is the point $q$.

**Answer: (B) $q$**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-04.title: Each digit in each place
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-04.body:
The numbers are $\overline{ABC}$, $\overline{BCD}$, $\overline{CDE}$, $\overline{DEA}$, $\overline{EAB}$. Each letter appears exactly once in the hundreds, once in the tens and once in the units place, so the sum is
$$111\,(A+B+C+D+E) = 2664 \Rightarrow A+B+C+D+E = 24.$$

**Answer: (C) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-06.title: Bound by $b^2$
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-06.body:
Since $a\ge1$ and $c\ge b$: $b^2\le bc\le abc = 10^6$, so $b\le1000$. Equality is possible: $a=1$, $b=c=1000$.

**Answer: (D) 1000**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-07.title: Weight of one dog
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-07.body:
One dog weighs $\frac KD$ kg, so $M$ dogs weigh $\frac{KM}{D}$ kg. This is the weight of $E$ elephants, so one elephant weighs $\frac{KM}{DE}$ kg.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-08.title: Second die matches
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-08.body:
Whatever colour the first die shows, the second die shows the same colour with probability $\frac26=\frac13$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac13$**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-09.title: Remainders mod 3
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-09.body:
$6n-1 = 3(2n-1)+2$ always leaves remainder 2 when divided by 3, so it is never divisible by 3.

The others can be: $n=1$ gives $5n+1=6$; $n=3$ gives $n^2=9$; $n=2$ gives $n(n+1)=6$ and $n^3-2=6$.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-10.title: Two isosceles triangles
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-10.body:
$AB = OB$ (both equal the radius), so triangle $ABO$ is isosceles and $\angle BOA = \angle BAO = 11°$. The exterior angle at $B$ is $\angle OBC = 22°$.

$OB=OC$, so triangle $OBC$ is isosceles and $\angle OCB = 22°$.

$\angle COD$ is an exterior angle of triangle $AOC$: $\angle COD = \angle CAO + \angle ACO = 11°+22° = 33°$.

**Answer: (C) 33°**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-11.title: Simulate option (D)
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-11.body:
Deal the deck OKAAONRG step by step:

| hand (top first) | moved to bottom | laid down |
|---|---|---|
| OKAAONRG | O | K |
| AAONRGO | A | A |
| ONRGOA | O | N |
| RGOAO | R | G |
| OAOR | O | A |
| ORO | O | R |
| OO | O | O |
| O | O | O |

The table reads KANGAROO ✓.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-11.title: Work backwards by positions
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-11.body:
Number the positions in the starting deck 1–8. Dealing removes positions in the order 2, 4, 6, 8, 3, 7, 5, 1 (track the positions through the dealing). So position 2 is K, 4 is A, 6 is N, 8 is G, 3 is A, 7 is R, 5 is O, 1 is O: the deck is O K A A O N R G.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-12.title: Parity and a construction
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-12.body:
Each coin must be turned an odd number of times, so the total number of turns, $3m$ after $m$ steps, is a sum of five odd numbers — odd. Hence $m$ is odd. $m=1$ turns only 3 coins, so $m\ge3$.

Three steps work: turn coins $\{1,2,3\}$, then $\{1,2,4\}$, then $\{1,2,5\}$: coins 1 and 2 are turned 3 times, coins 3, 4, 5 once. All show tails.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-13.title: Hidden faces
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-13.body:
Let a box have dimensions $a\times b\times c$, so its surface is $2(ab+bc+ca)$ and costs 1 litre.

In the construction there are three glued contacts, each along a whole face: the top box lies on a large face of a lower box, two boxes touch along a long side face, and one box touches the construction with its small end face. So one face of each kind is glued, and each glued contact hides two faces (one on each box):
$$\text{hidden area} = 2(ab+bc+ca) = \text{surface of one box}.$$
The construction needs $4-1=3$ litres.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-14.title: The sum is even
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-14.body:
Put $x=a-b$, $y=b-c$; then $c-a=-(x+y)$ and
$$x^2+y^2+(x+y)^2 = 2(x^2+xy+y^2),$$
which is even. So it can never equal **1**.

The others occur: $a=b=c$ gives 0; $(1,0,0)$ gives 2; $(2,1,0)$ gives 6; $(2,0,0)$ gives 8.

**Answer: (B) 1**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-15.title: Bounds
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-15.body:
The number $N$ satisfies $29\cdot10^{98}\le N<30\cdot10^{98}$, so
$$841\cdot10^{196}\le N^2<900\cdot10^{196},$$
i.e. $N^2$ is between $8.41\cdot10^{198}$ and $9\cdot10^{198}$. It has $199$ digits.

**Answer: (B) 199**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-16.title: Cuboctahedron
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-16.body:
$P$ has 12 vertices (one per cube edge). Cutting each corner of the cube leaves a triangular face (8 triangles), and each cube face leaves a square (6 squares): $F=14$.

Each triangle has 3 edges, and every edge of $P$ belongs to exactly one triangle: $E = 8\cdot3 = 24$. (Check with Euler: $12-24+14=2$ ✓.)

$E+F = 24+14 = 38$.

**Answer: (A) 38**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-17.title: Coordinates
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-17.body:
Put the square of area 9 at $[0,3]\times[0,3]$ on the ground; the square of area 1 sits on top of it in the right corner, $[2,3]\times[3,4]$.

One side of the large square passes through the top left corner $(0,3)$ of the square 9 and ends at the top left corner $(2,4)$ of the square 1: its slope is $\frac12$. Extending it down to the ground $y=0$, it reaches the lowest vertex of the large square at $(-6,0)$.

So the side of the large square goes from $(-6,0)$ to $(2,4)$: $s^2 = 8^2+4^2 = 80$.

**Answer: (B) 80**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-18.title: Parity pattern
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-18.body:
Parities: odd, odd, even, odd, odd, even, ... (odd + odd = even, odd + even = odd, even + odd = odd), repeating with period 3. The even terms are $f_3, f_6, f_9, \dots$

Among the first 2020 terms there are $\lfloor 2020/3\rfloor = 673$ of them.

**Answer: (A) 673**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-19.title: Radius and Pythagoras
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-19.body:
The circle touches the bottom side at $T$ (5 from the left corner, 4 from the right corner) and the left side. Its centre is above $T$ at distance $r$ from both sides, so $r=5$ and the centre is $(5,5)$ with the bottom left corner at the origin.

The circle passes through the top right vertex $(9,h)$:
$$(9-5)^2+(h-5)^2 = 25 \Rightarrow h-5 = 3 \Rightarrow h=8.$$
Area $= 9\cdot8 = 72$.

**Answer: (C) 72**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-20.title: Find the edges
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-20.body:
All three prisms have the same height $h$. The front left prism has depth 6; its top is 21, so its width is $\frac{21}6 = 3.5$; its front is 14, so $h = \frac{14}{3.5} = 4$.

The back prism has left face 16, so its depth is $\frac{16}4 = 4$; its top is 30, so its width (the full width) is $\frac{30}4 = 7.5$.

The front right prism therefore has width $7.5-3.5 = 4$ and depth 6: its top is $4\cdot6 = 24$.

**Answer: (B) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-21.title: Expected value
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-21.body:
If she always stops after $k$ cards, the red card is among them with probability $\frac k{10}$, so the expected win per game is
$$k\cdot\frac{10-k}{10}.$$
For $k=4,5,6,7,8$: $2.4,\ 2.5,\ 2.4,\ 2.1,\ 1.6$. The maximum is at $k=5$.

**Answer: (D) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-22.title: Read the signs
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-22.body:
- The graph meets the $y$-axis below the origin: $c<0$.
- It bends upward (it flattens out as it goes down to the right): $a>0$.
- At $x=0$ it is decreasing and the vertex lies to the right of the $y$-axis: $-\frac b{2a}>0$, so $b<0$.

Then $c<0$, $b+c<0$, $ac<0$, $ab<0$, but $bc>0$.

**Answer: (D) $bc$**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-24.title: Difference of two triangles
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-24.body:
The original garden $a\times b$ sits in the top left corner of the new one, $1.2a\times1.5b$ (or $1.5a\times1.2b$). Each diagonal cuts off a right triangle at the top left corner, and the shaded region is the big triangle minus the small one:
$$\frac{1.2a\cdot1.5b}{2}-\frac{ab}2 = \frac{0.8\,ab}{2} = 0.4\,ab = 30.$$
So $ab = 75$ m².

**Answer: (D) 75 m²**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-25.title: Rule out pairs
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-25.body:
If $N$ is divisible by two coprime numbers it is divisible by their product.

- (A) $N$ divisible by 4 and 9 would be divisible by 2 and 3. ✗
- (B) divisible by 10 means divisible by 5. ✗
- (C) divisible by 2 and 3 gives 6. ✗
- (E) divisible by 2 and 5 gives 10. ✗
- (D) $N = \text{lcm}(2,3,4,5,6,9,10,11) = 1980$ is divisible by none of 7, 8. ✓

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-26.title: Binomial coefficients
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-26.body:
Anna: $\binom{16}2 = 120$. Bella with $n$ flavours: $\binom n3 = 120$. Since $\binom{10}3 = \frac{10\cdot9\cdot8}{6} = 120$, $n=10$ and $16-10 = 6$ flavours were sold out.

**Answer: (E) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-27.title: Invariant mod 6
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-27.body:
Both 30 and 18 are multiples of 6, so the number of marbles in the box always leaves remainder $71 \bmod 6 = 5$. Hence there are always at least 5 marbles.

5 is reachable: $71\to41\to11\to29\to47\to17\to35\to5$ (taking out 30 or returning 18).

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-28.title: Subtract the folded triangles
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-28.body:
Let the square be $ABCD$ with diagonal $AC$, and fold the sides $CB$ and $CD$ onto the diagonal. The fold of $CB$ is the bisector of the $45°$ angle $BCA$; it meets $AB$ at $E$. Point $B$ lands on the diagonal at $B'$ with $CB'=CB=1$, and $EB'=EB$ with $EB'\perp AC$. Triangle $AB'E$ is a right isosceles triangle ($\angle EAB'=45°$), so $EB = EB' = AB' = \sqrt2-1$.

The quadrilateral $AECF$ is the square minus the two congruent triangles $CBE$ and $CDF$ (which are folded onto it):
$$1-2\cdot\frac{1\cdot(\sqrt2-1)}{2} = 2-\sqrt2.$$

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-29.title: Corner pyramid
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-29.body:
The visible part is a corner of the cube cut off by a plane: a pyramid with three mutually perpendicular edges 24, 25 and 27. Its volume is
$$\frac{24\cdot25\cdot27}{6} = 2700 \text{ m}^3.$$
This is 10% of the cube: $a^3 = 27\,000$, so $a = 30$ m.

**Answer: (A) 30 m**

kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-30.title: Pascal's triangle
kangaroo-ca-2020-g1112-30.body:
The exponents follow Pascal's triangle: a box in row $k$ (bottom row $k=0$) above $p_j,\dots,p_{j+k}$ equals $\prod_{i=0}^k p_{j+i}^{\binom ki}$. So $\alpha_i = \binom{n-1}{i-1}$, and $\alpha_2 = n-1 = 8$ gives $n=9$.

A box in row $k$ starting at position $j$ ($1\le j\le 9-k$) contains $p_4$ when $j\le4\le j+k$. Counting row by row for $k=0,\dots,8$:
$$1+2+3+4+4+4+3+2+1 = 24.$$

**Answer: (C) 24**
